subject: Prompt capture: scope, storage locations, and retention (post-demo recap)

Subject: Post-demo recap — what Medinet needs to know about prompt/response storage

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for your time this morning — great conversation and appreciate the specificity on the workflows. Per our notes, I wanted to capture what we agreed and next steps so your legal and infra teams have a single reference.

Key takeaways (short):
- Capture scope: Medinet wants to ensure PII is not persisted from patient-facing prompts unless explicitly opted-in. For named-patient flows (support chat), you want only anonymized telemetry stored.
- Storage locations: Hosted Redwood API (us-west region) by default; for regulated flows you asked about VPC/private deployment options.
- Retention: You requested TTLs and an option for session-only (ephemeral) vs persisted for 90/365-day buckets.
- Logging controls: Need access to audit logs (token-level redaction) and ability to turn on/off prompt capture per route.

Action items I promised:
1) Internal confirmation from our security team on exactly which fields we persist in our telemetry (full matrix).
2) Suggested retention buckets and API knobs to control per-route capture.
3) Example entry in our SOC2 evidence demonstrating retention deletions.

Looping in Marissa (CS) to coordinate the short technical note and Jordan (security/solutions) for the exact capture matrix.

Next step: Jordan will reply with the matrix + recommended default TTLs by EOD Monday. Marissa will set up a follow-up call next week with your infra and legal.

Hi Priya —

Following up with the capture matrix and concrete answers. Below is a concise mapping of "what gets stored, where, and for how long" for Redwood's hosted offering (us-west) and our Private/VPC option.

1) Prompt inputs (text payloads)
- Hosted (default): by default we persist prompts for diagnostic telemetry only when capture is enabled per-route. When persisted, they are stored in encrypted object storage in the same region (us-west) and can be configured to TTL at 30/90/365 days.
- Private (VPC): prompts may be routed to customer-managed storage; Redwood will not persist in our hosted store unless agreed.

2) Model outputs (generated tokens)
- Hosted: outputs are treated the same as prompts for capture — persisted only if route-level capture enabled. Outputs that are flagged as PII by our optional redaction hook are replaced with token placeholders in stored logs.

3) Transient session data (KV cache, in-memory)
- Not persisted to disk by default; per-session artifacts are ephemeral and cleared on session termination.

4) Audit logs / access logs
- Access logs and API request metadata (timestamps, model used, token counts, route id) are stored for 365 days to support billing and SLA investigations. Full request/response payloads are not included unless capture is enabled.

5) PII redaction and field-level masking
- We offer a pre-ingest redaction hook that can be configured to remove or hash defined fields (SSNs, MRNs, etc.). When enabled, the redacted payload is what gets persisted.

Suggested defaults for Medinet (based on today's discussion):
- Patient-facing chat: capture disabled by default; if enabled for debugging, TTL=30 days, redaction hook enabled.
- Batch inference for reporting: capture enabled, TTL=365 days, encrypted at rest with KMS.

Compliance/attestation references: our SOC2 snapshot (attached) describes deletion practices and key controls. For Private deployments, we can provide a playbook for retention policies and proof-of-deletion scripts.

- Priya/Legal: confirm which specific fields Medinet requires to be considered PII so we can map to the redaction hook.
- I'll prepare a short "capture matrix" spreadsheet and a sample API config to flip capture per-route.

Thanks Jordan — this is helpful and already answers a lot. Two clarifying questions from Legal and infra:

1) For hosted capture when TTL=30 days, do you also remove all backups/snapshots that might contain the data? We need assurance that retained data is purged from backups and long-term imaging.
2) For the redaction hook, can you confirm whether hashing is reversible within Redwood (i.e., is it deterministic reversible or one-way)? We need to know if Medinet can request de-identified data that still allows re-linking by our key.

If you can include brief answers we can share with our CISO and legal. Also please add a short note about how deletions are audited (request IDs, logs).

Hi Priya — following up with the two clarifications Monday afternoon. Apologies for the slightly longer note; want to be precise so legal has what it needs.

1) Backups/snapshots: For hosted deployments, our standard snapshot lifecycle does not retain application-layer persisted captures beyond the configured TTL. When a TTL-triggered deletion occurs, we also mark associated snapshot objects for deletion and run a secondary purge process. We maintain a deletion audit record (deletion request id, timestamp, object ids). For higher-assurance requests we can run an expunge job that removes objects and marks the snapshot metadata; this is what we would recommend for regulated datasets. We document this in our SOC2 runbook and can provide a redaction/deletion playbook to Medinet.

2) Hashing vs one-way redaction: Our redaction hook supports two modes:
- One-way hash: irreversible (recommended for PHI where re-linking is not desired).
- Deterministic HMAC (reversible with customer key): keyed-HMAC with customer-provided key — allows Medinet to re-link when you hold the key. For Private/VPC deployments, it is straightforward to ensure the key never leaves your environment.

Auditing deletions: Deletion actions generate a unique request id that is logged to the audit trail (who requested, scope, affected object ids). Audit logs themselves are retained for 365 days and are accessible to your security team on request (or via our console with role-based access).

Attachments: I'm attaching the updated capture matrix that includes the TTL columns and a short example API snippet that shows the per-route capture toggle.

If this matches what you're looking for, Marissa can lock in the infra/legal call for Wednesday.

Thanks —
